skill.name: detection-sigma
skill.description: Create, validate, convert, and document Sigma detection rules for SIEM, threat hunting, ATT&CK mapping, and compliance monitoring workflows.
skill.summary: Build portable Sigma detections for SIEM, threat hunting, and compliance monitoring.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Sigma rule examples, MITRE ATT&CK references, public documentation links, and SIEM query snippets. I found one contextual issue: a deployment example uses placeholder administrator credentials and disables TLS verification, which should be revised before publication. No prompt injection or malicious execution instructions were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The Splunk deployment example uses literal administrator credentials and disables TLS verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use secret manager or environment variable placeholders, require TLS verification, and mark any insecure lab-only option clearly.

remediation.issue: The package references helper scripts that are not present in the scanned file tree.
remediation.suggestion: Include the scripts with secure argument handling or revise the documentation to use pySigma commands available to users.

remediation.issue: Detection examples include sensitive attack technique names that trigger automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep defensive framing near those examples and avoid runnable offensive payloads or step-by-step attacker commands.

content.value_statement: Security teams need portable detection logic across different SIEM tools. This skill guides Sigma rule creation, validation, conversion, ATT&CK mapping, and compliance monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Sigma rules for process, network, file, registry, DNS, and authentication logs.
Provides MITRE ATT&CK technique mappings and detection pattern examples.
Explains SIEM backend syntax for Splunk, Elastic, Sentinel, QRadar, and EQL.
Includes compliance-focused templates for PCI DSS, NIST 800-53, and ISO 27001 monitoring.
Documents Sigma field modifiers, backend support limits, and tuning guidance.
Provides reusable templates for credential access, lateral movement, persistence, and privilege escalation detections.
limitations: The referenced Python conversion and validation scripts are not included in this package.
Rules require environment-specific log source and field mapping validation.
Detection examples must be tuned before production deployment to reduce false positives.
Some Sigma modifiers have partial backend support and may need manual changes.

use_cases.title: Create Portable Detections
use_cases.description: Design Sigma rules that can be reviewed, versioned, and converted for multiple SIEM platforms.

use_cases.title: Build Threat Hunts
use_cases.description: Translate ATT&CK techniques into structured hunting logic with log sources, fields, and false positive notes.

use_cases.title: Map Compliance Monitoring
use_cases.description: Connect audit and monitoring controls to Sigma rule templates for PCI DSS, NIST, and ISO 27001 evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Starter Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sigma rule for suspicious encoded PowerShell activity. Include log source, fields, ATT&CK tags, false positives, and test guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Tune A Detection
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this detection goal and propose Sigma selections, filters, field modifiers, severity, and tuning notes for a Windows enterprise environment.

prompt_templates.title: Convert For SIEMs
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare conversion guidance for a Sigma rule targeting Splunk, Elastic, and Microsoft Sentinel. Highlight field mapping risks and backend limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detection coverage plan for credential access and lateral movement. Map ATT&CK techniques, required logs, Sigma templates, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Create a rule for repeated failed logons mapped to PCI DSS.
output_examples.output: A Sigma rule outline with authentication log sources, failed logon events, PCI tags, key fields, false positive notes, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a PowerShell detection before Sentinel deployment.
output: Confirms required Windows process creation logs.
Recommends precise image and command-line matching.
Lists Sentinel field mapping checks before deployment.

output_examples.input: Plan coverage for credential access techniques.
output_examples.output: A coverage matrix with ATT&CK techniques, log sources, Sigma template choices, tuning priorities, and gaps that need new telemetry.

best_practices: Validate each Sigma rule against representative historical logs before production deployment.
Map every rule to ATT&CK techniques, log sources, and known false positive scenarios.
Keep rule changes in version control with peer review and deployment history.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy generated rules without testing field mappings in the target SIEM.
Do not copy sample credentials, endpoints, or TLS settings into production automation.
Do not rely on broad keyword matches when precise field modifiers are available.

faq.question: What is Sigma?
faq.answer: Sigma is a vendor-neutral rule format for describing log-based security detections across SIEM and analytics platforms.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy rules automatically?
faq.answer: It provides deployment guidance and examples, but the scanned package does not include deployment scripts.

faq.question: Which SIEM platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The references discuss Splunk, Elasticsearch, Microsoft Sentinel, QRadar, EQL, Chronicle, and related pySigma backends.

faq.question: Does this replace detection testing?
faq.answer: No. Generated rules still need validation with local logs, expected alerts, and false positive review.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates and mappings for PCI DSS, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 style monitoring.

faq.question: Why do examples mention offensive techniques?
faq.answer: They are used as defensive detection targets and ATT&CK mappings, not as instructions to perform attacks.
